speaker: Doctor

DIAGNOSIS READY: Pemphigus Foliaceus.

The presence of desmoglein antibodies confirms an autoimmune blistering disease. Since your skin biopsy shows subcorneal acantholysis (likely causing crusting rather than large fluid-filled blisters) and direct immunofluorescence is positive for intercellular IgG and C3, but you lack the severe mucosal involvement seen in Pemphigus Vulgaris, this is consistent with Pemphigus Foliaceus.
